newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close down on blue-chip losses.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close down on blue-chip losses.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended marginally lower on Monday despite active local buying of secondliners due to foreign selling of selected blue-chips, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 1.23 points, or 0.23 percent, to close at 542.52 points after touching a low of 540.36 points. Losers led gainers by 49 to 48, with 50 counters unchanged.

"The was no direction in the market today, many traders just adopted one-day transactions. They bought and then sold it for just small gains. I don't think there was any real buying," said one local broker.
Brokers said local-led active buying failed to push the composite index up as foreigners offloaded some big- and medium-capitalised stocks.
They said Bakrie Brothers, Bimantara Citra, Citra Marga and Sampoerna were among the key stocks sold.

Plantation and telecommunications firm Bakrie Brothers fell 75 rupiah to 2,725 on a turnover of 1.3 million shares. Brokers said the fall was due to profit-taking after it made significant gains for the last week on strong first-half results.
Heavy equipment and spare-part firm Intraco Penta topped the active list. It rose 225 rupiah to 1,725 on a volume of 11.3 million shares.
Brokers said the rise was due to reports saying the company had expressed interest in acquiring a stake in a heavy equipment distributor and also plans to a stock split.
Secondliners Rimba Niaga, Voksel Electric and Summarecon were alseo active on what brokers said was speculative buying.
Textile firm Rimba Niaga rose 275 rupiah, or 28.21 percent to 1,250 rupiah on a volume of 1.2 million shares.
